questions.q: What is the best way to think about equity?
options: A pile of cash the owners can spend at any time
A type of liability owed to shareholders
A residual claim equal to Assets minus Liabilities
The total revenue a business has earned over its lifetime
questions.explain: Equity is whatever is left over for the owners once every liability is subtracted from every asset — a residual, not a cash balance.

questions.q: If a business's assets are entirely financed by liabilities, what is its equity?
options: It is impossible to have zero equity
Zero — there is nothing left over for the owners
questions.explain: Equity = Assets - Liabilities. If liabilities equal assets, equity is zero, even though the business clearly holds assets.

questions.q: How is equity typically labeled in a sole proprietorship?
options: A separate capital account for each partner
There is no equity in a sole proprietorship
questions.explain: A sole proprietorship usually tracks equity in a single Owner's Capital account, sometimes paired with an Owner's Drawing account.

questions.q: Thornbury Analytics Inc. starts the year with $200,000 in Retained Earnings, earns $70,000 in net income, and pays $20,000 in dividends. What is the ending Retained Earnings balance?
questions.explain: $200,000 + $70,000 net income - $20,000 dividends = $250,000 ending Retained Earnings.

questions.q: What does Oracle Fusion General Ledger do with revenue and expense accounts at year-end?
options: It deletes them permanently with no further record
It automatically closes them into Retained Earnings as part of the year-end close process
It converts them directly into liabilities
questions.explain: As part of the year-end close, revenue and expense accounts are closed into Retained Earnings, reflecting the period's net income.
